one_sentence_fix: Add a second independent corroborating source for the gas-turbine backlog claim (currently single-sourced to Alaska Public Media, not a primary source) to bring all four rebuttal points to primary or dual-outlet standard.

criteria.name: Hook strength
criteria.notes: First line names Governor Dunleavy, quotes the verbatim price, gives the scale (100 to 500 MW through 2027); correction signal lands on line 3, just inside the see-more window.

criteria.name: Claim load-bearing + AK stakes
criteria.notes: Anchors hyperscaler siting for 100 to 500 MW through 2026-27; correction names the concrete failure mode. Matches dossier ak_stakes.

criteria.name: Steelman fairness
criteria.notes: Two paragraphs genuinely steelman the claim before the rebuttal. 'Worth a flight to Anchorage' is mild dry wit, not snark.

criteria.name: Counter-evidence quality
criteria.notes: Three of four rebuttal points are primary (GaffneyCline via House Finance, Giessel, Chugach). Turbine-backlog point is single non-primary (Alaska Public Media).

criteria.name: Factual density
criteria.notes: Named specifics in nearly every sentence: names, dates, dollar figures, MW, outlets.

criteria.name: Source quality
criteria.notes: Claim attributed to Dunleavy with two independent appearances; counter-evidence three primary plus one credible secondary, all in dossier.

criteria.name: Voice match
criteria.notes: Analytical, structural, business-literate, corrective not contemptuous. No banned phrases or influencer cadence.

criteria.name: Readability (LinkedIn)
criteria.notes: Tight 2-4 sentence paragraphs, one 3-item bullet block, 455 words, under 3000 chars.

criteria.name: Engagement question
criteria.notes: Real debatable binary tied to the corrected frame, no CTA.

criteria.name: Business actionability
criteria.notes: Allocator can name three gap-checks (financial close, certified timeline, turbine supply) to reframe the price from floor to contingency.
